author: Robin Houston
title: Squares of squares, and the group of rational points on the circle
note: 2 August 2016; formulations P4 and W1; accessed 2 October 2026
tex: R. Houston, \emph{Squares of squares, and the group of rational points on the circle}, Bosker Blog, 2 August 2016, formulations P4 and W1. \url{https://bosker.wordpress.com/2016/08/02/squares-of-squares-and-the-group-of-rational-points-on-the-circle/}. Accessed 2 October 2026.

review: Complete primary post read. Its formulations are not an exclusion theorem for the finite frequency family treated here.

author: {Magic Squares of Squares project}
title: Excluding every two-block center
note: Public unrefereed research note; theorem statement accessed 2 October 2026
tex: Magic Squares of Squares project, \emph{Excluding every two-block center}, public unrefereed research note (2026). \url{https://github.com/uwe-schwarz/magic-squares-of-squares/blob/main/research/prime-support/two-block-exponent-one.md}. Accessed 2 October 2026.
support: The note explicitly claims a uniform exclusion for actual two-prime central roots with arbitrary positive exponents. It is not a premise of this paper, whose main exclusion concerns a restricted frequency family over the larger rational-circle domain.
review: Primary theorem statement, status, and starting Gaussian hypotheses read through GitHub. The entire proof, in particular its later descent, was not audited in this editorial pass. The claim is described as a claim, not an accepted stronger theorem.
